title: Credit-card purchases and refund options
text: Curated paraphrase of public guidance, reviewed 2026-10-17. For problems with a credit-card purchase, start by asking the seller to resolve the issue. The card issuer can explain applicable dispute options. Different problems and payment products have different conditions; this reference does not determine a customer's eligibility or establish that any refund happened.

title: Keeping evidence for a credit-card billing dispute
text: Curated paraphrase of public guidance, reviewed 2026-10-17. Retain copies of dispute correspondence and a dated log of follow-up calls. Billing errors and defective-merchandise disputes can involve different processes. Consult the original guidance and applicable card agreement; this application does not calculate legal deadlines or determine dispute rights.

title: Refund tracing reference types
text: Curated paraphrase of provider-specific documentation, reviewed 2026-10-17. Supported refund flows may expose an Acquirer Reference Number (ARN), System Trace Audit Number (STAN), or Retrieval Reference Number (RRN) to help trace a refund. Reference availability depends on the network and payment method. A reference does not independently prove a customer's bank posted a credit; this provider's behavior is not universal policy.

title: Refund states, partial refunds, and failures
text: Curated paraphrase of provider-specific documentation, reviewed 2026-10-17. Refunds may cover part of a purchase and may be pending or fail. A merchant-side refund record and the customer-visible credit are different evidence sources. Failed refund handling and processing behavior depend on the payment method and provider; do not apply these details as a fictional merchant's contractual policy.
